<details>
This PKGBUILD is straightforward and poses no risk for the narrow operations of `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.

**Top-level code analysis**: The file only contains variable assignments at the global scope (pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, pkgdesc, arch, url, license, depends, makedepends, options, conflicts, source, sha256sums). There is no `pkgver()` function, no command substitution, no `eval`, and no other top-level code that would execute during sourcing.

**Source fetching**: The `source` array downloads a single tarball from the package's own declared upstream GitHub repository (`github.com/erickochen/purple`) at a specific tag (`v3.27.0`). A proper SHA256 checksum is provided (not SKIP), so the downloaded archive will be verified.

**Out of scope for this gate**: The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions will not execute during `--nobuild --noprepare`. They contain only standard Rust/Cargo build operations (cargo fetch, cargo build, install commands), which will be audited in the full review.

No evidence of injected malicious code, obfuscation, suspicious network destinations, or data exfiltration.
</details>
<evidence>

Standard PKGBUILD with proper checksum and upstream source, safe for sourcing and fetching.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
